Elaine (AE): Hey team — pre-PoC checklist for AcmeCorp. They want Private deployment in our VPC with a handoff to their firewall team. Question: should we recommend VPC peering or interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for the control plane and egress? Also need a short list of firewall rules, SLOs, and any pricing caveats to share with procurement.

Raj (SE): For control plane & API traffic -> prefer PrivateLink (interface endpoints). Simpler for cross-account connectivity, no route table changes. For high-throughput model inference traffic you can do peering if you need direct VPC-level routing, but that requires careful CIDR planning.

Raj (SE): Quick bullet: PrivateLink = per-ENI interface in customer's VPC, preserves TLS, fewer routing changes. Peering = LAN-style connectivity, lower latency for very high throughput but NO support for security group endpointing the same way.

Tom (NetOps): @Raj can you confirm egress NAT behavior? Customer cares about keeping client IP for auditing. If traffic flows through our egress, are we able to map a stable IP per-customer?

Raj (SE): If you terminate to our connector (our side outbound), we can advertise a stable egress EIP per-tenant on Dedicated/Private. With PrivateLink the customer's source IP will be the connector's ENI unless they use direct peering. So if they need original client srcIP visible in logs, peering + source preservation at their NAT is the path.

Tom (NetOps): Understood. So two options: 1) Peering + preserve client IP (they must ensure non-overlapping CIDRs). 2) PrivateLink + we provide static egress IP(s) they whitelist.

Maria (Cust): Are there specific firewall ports/protocols we should give to our firewall team? They run strict outbound policies.

Raj (SE): Minimal list (TCP): `443` outbound to our PrivateLink ENI or peered subnets. If features include streaming/websockets: `TCP 443` still, we keep ALPN/TLS. If using metrics or agent heartbeats to our control plane: `UDP 123` (NTP) optionally and `TCP 443` to metrics endpoints.

Raj (SE): Example allowlist snippet for firewall team:
```
# Allow to Redwood Private endpoints (example)
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: <privatelink-interface-eni-ip-range> or <our-egress-eip>
```

Tom (NetOps): Also call out SNI/TLS inspect note: if they TLS-inspect (MITM) the SNI will be rewritten and our mTLS (if requested) or cert pinning may fail. Recommend allowing passthrough for sessions to `*.redwood-inference.net` if they want full integrity.

SecurityBot: Attachments requested by our security policy: network diagram (customer and redwood), data flow model, encryption at transit/rest statements, KMS/HSM integration doc, SOC2 + pen test summary. Provide those to the customer security questionnaire.

Elaine (AE): Thanks — Raj, Tom, can you assemble a one-pager with: recommended topology options (PrivateLink vs peering), minimal firewall allowlist, egress IP options and a short pricing note for Reserved vs Burstable capacity? Need by EOD to send to procurement. @Maria, any timeline?

Maria (Cust): Procurement wants the networking doc and a ballpark for egress bandwidth costs. POC starts next Tues. EOD would be great.

Sam (Eng): Pricing callout: Hosted vs Private deploy differences — data egress and provisioned GPU hours matter. For Private deployments we charge a base platform fee + reserved capacity price (monthly) and there's an additional per-GB egress if they exceed included transfer. For a short estimate give their expected tokens/sec or average rps and we can convert to bandwidth.

Raj (SE): One more operational note: if they plan to use on-prem proxies (forward proxy with outbound TLS termination), ensure `CONNECT` and `TLS passthrough` are supported or they will need our explicit proxy support. Also certs: if mutual TLS is required we will exchange certs during the handoff.

Tom (NetOps): I'll draft the allowlist with examples of CIDR/EIP placeholders and a NAT diagram. Will include peering caveats: no overlapping CIDRs, and route table entries required.

Elaine (AE): Perfect. I'll combine into a single PDF. Raj — can you drop the PrivateLink ENI sample output and a short note on failover (fallback to hosted cluster in another region) — customer asked about SLA and graceful degradation.

Raj (SE): Yes — we recommend a multi-tier fallback: primary = Private deployment in customer VPC, fallback = our hosted model variant (compatible model) in different region with higher latency but lower cost. We'll include config snippet for canary/failover policy.

Raj (SE): Snippet: `failover_policy: { primary: private-deploy, fallback: hosted-us-east-1, health_check: 5s }`

Elaine (AE): Thanks all — I'll send draft to Maria and procurement once Tom & Raj upload the diagrams. :thumbsup:

Maria (Cust): Appreciate the fast turnaround. We'll review tonight and get back with any security questionnaire gaps.
